name: California
one: California mails a ballot to every registered voter. Below: how to send it back and the deadlines.
sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in California, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Getting your ballot

Monday, October 19Passed

No request is needed: ballots go out automatically. To have your ballot mailed to a different address (for example a college address), the state's student guide says to update your registration by Monday, October 19, 2026. That date has passed; contact your county election office about a replacement ballot. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

By mail: postmarked on or before Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and received by your county election office by Tuesday, November 10, 2026. Dropped off in person or at a drop box: by 8:00 p.m. on November 3, 2026. (official page)

That date has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. When and where to vote early.

California’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in California or in another state? What California says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. Every active registered voter in California is mailed a ballot. Any registered voter may vote by mail instead of going to the polls. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Automatically. You do not need to ask. County election offices had to start mailing a ballot to every active registered voter by October 5, 2026. Check your mailing address and status with the state's My Voter Status tool. Open it (official page)
  • A replacement ballot. If your ballot never came, or you lost or ruined it, ask your county election office for a replacement: on the state's form, or by phone, email or fax. Only you may ask for your own replacement ballot. Voting locations also hand out replacement ballots. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Missed the October 19 registration deadline? From October 20 through Election Day you can register and vote at your county election office, a vote center or a polling place. This is called Same Day (conditional) Voter Registration, and you vote a provisional ballot. Open it (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. The return envelope has First-Class postage already paid. The state recommends mailing it at least 7 days before Election Day. If you mail it closer to Election Day, take it to a U.S. Post Office and ask a postal employee for a hand-stamped postmark. (official page)
  • Drop box. Any official ballot drop box or drop-off location in your county, open October 5 through 8:00 p.m. on November 3, 2026. Find one at caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov. (official page)
  • In person. Any polling place, vote center or county election office in California by 8:00 p.m. on November 3, 2026. (official page)
  • Someone else for you. Anyone may return your ballot for you, as long as they are not paid per ballot. Fill in the authorization section on the outside of the return envelope. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Fill in everything asked on the return envelope and sign it. Your county compares your signature with the one on your registration; if it is missing or does not match, the county contacts you with a form to fix it. If this is your first federal election and you did not give a driver license, state ID or Social Security number when you registered, send your county a copy of an ID (a recent utility bill, a government letter, a passport, a student ID and the like) before the election. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on California’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Monday, October 5, 2026 to Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

Early voting sites opened October 5, 2026. In counties that use vote centers, the vote centers open by Saturday, October 24, 2026. On Election Day, polls are open 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. (official page)

Students

At school in California, away from home

A Californian away at a college, trade school or technical school in California may register at either the school address (dorm students use the residence hall address) or the usual home address. The school address puts the local contests of the school's county on your ballot; the home address, those of your home county. You do not need to live there any set length of time first. You may not register or vote in two places in the same election. To get your ballot at the other address, change your registration's mailing address (to the school, home or a P.O. box). (official page)

At school in another state, with California as home

The state's pages do not speak separately to students at school in another U.S. state. They say a Californian away at school chooses which address to register at, may not register in two places in the same election, and can have the ballot mailed to a different mailing address. A student living outside the United States can register with the Federal Post Card Application or the state's online registration, and is then treated as an overseas voter. (official page)

Military and overseas

Register or ask for your ballot with California's online registration or the federal FPCA form, and choose to get your ballot by mail, fax or email. Mail it back postmarked by Election Day and received within 7 days after (by November 10, 2026). The state suggests sending it by September 29 from a ship at sea, October 4 from outside the U.S., or October 23 from inside the U.S. A voter outside the U.S. may fax it back (with an oath form) so it arrives by 8:00 p.m. on November 3; a voted ballot may not be emailed. (official page)

California in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The registration deadline (October 19, 2026) has passed, but Same Day Voter Registration is open through Election Day at county offices, vote centers and polling places.
  • Statewide help line: (800) 345-VOTE (8683), the Secretary of State's voter hotline.
  • Local details (drop box and vote center locations, how to get a replacement ballot) are set by each county election office.
Where this comes from: 6 pages of California’s election office, its laws and the federal guide

  3. 2026 General Election College Student Voter Resource Guide, California Secretary of State, Students Vote Project (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  4. Vote-by-Mail Ballot Return Frequently Asked Questions, California Secretary of State (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  5. College Students and Voters Living Abroad, California Secretary of State (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  6. Military & Overseas Voters, California Secretary of State (official page; read October 21, 2026)

Checked October 21, 2026. Rules and dates can change: California’s election office, and your county or local election office, have the final word.
